tools.name: account
tools.description: This API key: tier, limits and usage this month.

tools.name: list_samples
tools.description: Precomputed real outputs (no upload needed): ids, titles, sizes, download URLs.

tools.name: get_sample
tools.description: One sample: README, licence, channels_used, and its embeddings in the POST /v1/embeddings response format (first windows only for long ones).

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Start an upload of a local .edf, .bdf or .npy file (at most 2 GB). Returns id and a presigned upload_url: PUT the file there within 10 minutes with exactly upload_headers (e.g. curl -X PUT --upload-file night.edf -H 'Content-Length: N' '<upload_url>', no Authorization header), then call start_embedd

tools.name: start_embedding_job
tools.description: Queue an embeddings job on an uploaded file. window_seconds: 2 to 30 (default 30); stride_seconds: default window_seconds. picks: EDF/BDF channel labels to keep; channel_names: 10-20 labels overriding the file's; sfreq: required for .npy. Bills 30 s of EEG per window at any window_seconds (refunded

tools.name: start_sleep_staging_job
tools.description: Queue sleep staging of an uploaded whole-night PSG (.edf/.bdf; >= 1 EEG channel with a 10-20 label at >= 100 Hz; EOG used if present). eeg_channel/eog_channel: channels for the YASA features; picks, channel_names as for embeddings. Counts 1 night of the weekly quota (refunded on failure). Poll get_j

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: A job's status (queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, expired), usage, error or result. Poll every 5 s while queued or running.

tools.name: get_result_url
tools.description: Fresh presigned GET URLs (10 minutes) of a succeeded job's result. Embeddings: .npy float32 [windows, 768], window i starts at i * t_start_step s. Sleep staging: url = hypnogram JSON (stage, probabilities, confidence per 30 s epoch), csv_url = CSV, plus the summary.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_upload" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_samples, get_sample, get_result_url · Private data: account, create_upload, start_embedding_job · Public sink: list_samples, get_sample, create_upload · Destructive: get_sample.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_samples, get_sample, get_result_url · Private data: account, create_upload, start_embedding_job · Public sink: list_samples, get_sample, create_upload · Destructive: get_sample

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
